Nema vs Glean

The short answer

Glean is built around permission-aware enterprise search, a company knowledge layer, and governed agents that work across business systems. Glean also has a substantial Slack experience. Users can ask questions, receive answers grounded in company knowledge, summarize conversations, and run agent workflows. Nema takes a lighter, channel-centered approach. Each Slack channel gets a coworker configured for that team's work.

Choose Glean when broad enterprise discovery and governance are the main requirements. Choose Nema when a team wants to start with a bounded channel coworker and keep requests, corrections, and approvals in its Slack threads.

An account brief example

A customer success channel needs a renewal brief. The inputs include commitments from channel threads, approved account notes, a contract summary, and support history. The brief must cite evidence, distinguish known concerns from inferred risk, and name follow-up owners.

With Nema, the customer channel keeps the account-specific guidance and review in Slack. The coworker uses the allowed records, posts a draft in the thread, and lets the account team correct it. Any proposed update can wait for the named approver. The channel retains the team's correction for the next brief.

Glean can search a much broader company knowledge base while respecting the requester's source permissions. Its Slack app can answer questions from past messages and connected enterprise content. Glean Agents extend that context into workflows, and the company now documents independent agents with their own identities, activity records, and governance.

Choose Nema when

Choose Nema when the company wants to begin with a specific operating channel rather than deploy a broad enterprise search layer. Teams can establish explicit instructions, context, tools, and approvers one channel at a time. That can make ownership easy to see for recurring work such as account reviews or weekly operating reports.

Nema also offers model choice and a shared Slack interface. Confirm the required connections and administrative controls in the current product before a wider rollout.

Choose Glean when

Choose Glean when employees need reliable discovery across a large set of company systems. Glean's main advantage is its mature permission-aware search and knowledge platform, backed by enterprise governance. Its current material advertises more than 275 connectors and supports search, chat, and agents in Slack.

Glean is also the stronger documented fit for organizations that need agent identity, broad auditability, independent agents, and deployment across Slack, Jira, Teams, and other apps. Its wider scope usually calls for more planning around content access and indexing.

Test permissions and freshness

Run the same account brief under two users with different permissions. Check whether each product excludes records the requester cannot see, shows useful citations, and reports stale or missing data. Then give an agent its own service identity and inspect the audit trail for a proposed write.

Ask how quickly source changes appear and how admins remove a source. For Glean, review connector indexing and real-time access behavior. For Nema, verify the exact connected read and action. Permission-aware marketing claims still need a product test against the systems your company uses.

Common questions

Does Glean work inside Slack?

Yes. Glean offers an official Slack experience for questions, grounded answers, conversation summaries, and selected agent workflows. Both products support shared work in Slack.

Is Nema an enterprise search replacement?

No broad replacement claim is appropriate. Nema can use permitted channel context and connected sources for specific jobs. Glean is designed to index and search enterprise knowledge across many systems.

Which is faster to start?

Nema's channel-by-channel setup may be smaller for a bounded team workflow. Glean can deliver wider discovery but requires decisions about connectors, permissions, and governance. Actual rollout time depends on the source systems and controls required.
